business.profile: Business = help the learner work in companies, meetings, sales, operations and professional communication.
avoid: buzzwords
investor jargon without broad business value
rare MBA-style terminology
level_policy: Business should mostly live in B1-B2 with a useful C1 layer for professional communication.
A1 should be minimal because very basic words are already covered by CEFR core.

travel.profile: Travel = help the learner travel independently before, during and after a trip, including real problems and service situations.
avoid: poetic travel words
tourism marketing words
rare geography terms
broad environment words unless directly useful during travel
tech/web words unless directly needed for booking or check-in
weak holiday-only words
level_policy: Travel may contain many A1-A2 survival words, but after the first 80-100 words prefer B1-B2 practical terms.
C1-C2 should be almost zero unless the word is highly practical for travel.
Do not fill with low-value C1-C2 words just to look advanced.

technology.profile: Technology = help the learner understand modern tech, apps, devices, digital services and support contexts.
avoid: deep engineering jargon unless common in everyday tech work or product communication
brand names
random library names
level_policy: Technology should lean B1-B2 because useful tech vocabulary is often above basic English.
Keep C1-C2 small and practical.

health.profile: Health = help the learner talk to doctors, understand symptoms, treatment, pharmacy and basic medical information.
avoid: rare Latin disease names
diagnostic jargon that a normal patient will not hear
high-stakes specialist terminology unless very common
level_policy: Health can include many A2-B1 patient communication words.
Specialized medical words are allowed only when useful for real doctor/pharmacy interactions.

education.profile: Education = help the learner study, communicate at school/university and understand learning contexts.
avoid: rare pedagogy theory unless useful for real student/teacher communication
university bureaucracy that is too country-specific
level_policy: Education should mostly be A2-B2.
C1 terms are allowed for academic work if useful, but C2 should be avoided for this category.

law.profile: Law = help the learner understand legal work, client communication, courts, contracts and legal documents.
avoid: rare doctrinal theory unless genuinely useful for legal practice or reading legal documents
country-specific procedural terms unless broadly useful
Latin maxims unless common in legal English
level_policy: Law is a professional category: most words should be B2-C1, with a smaller B1 practical layer.
A1-A2 should be almost absent except unavoidable general words used in legal settings.
C2 is allowed more than in lifestyle categories, but only for useful legal reading/work vocabulary.

finance.profile: Finance = help the learner handle money, banking, accounting, payments and financial documents.
avoid: obscure derivatives jargon unless category is specifically trading/investing
rare accounting-only labels unless useful in documents
level_policy: Finance should lean B1-B2, with a meaningful C1 layer for documents and professional contexts.

software_development.profile: Software Development = help the learner work as a software developer in English.
avoid: very rare framework internals
obscure algorithms unless common at work
random library names
overly academic computer science terms unless useful in developer communication
level_policy: Software development should mostly be B1-C1.
A1 should be avoided because the category should feel professional, not basic CEFR.
C2 is allowed only for genuinely useful expert terms.

trading.profile: Trading = help the learner understand markets, investing and trading communication.
avoid: meme-trading slang
ultra-obscure indicators
platform-specific slang
level_policy: Trading is intentionally more specialized than ordinary finance.
Most words should be B2-C1, with some B1 foundations.
